He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]]. ==College career== McGruder, a 6'4" shooting guard from [[Landover, Maryland]], was an [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] teammate of [[Michael Beasley]]'s and followed Beasley's path to [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] to play for coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]]. McGruder started for three seasons for the Wildcats. As a sophomore in [[2010–11 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|2010–11]], McGruder teamed with backcourt mate [[Jacob Pullen]] to lead the Wildcats to a third place [[Big 12 Conference]] finish. McGruder averaged 11.1 [[Points per game|points]] and a team-best 5.9 [[rebounds per game]].{{cite web | title = Kansas State Bio | work = KStateSports.com | url = http://www.kstatesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/mcgruder_rodney00.html | accessdate = March 3, 2013 | archive-date = December 17, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121217010115/http://www.kstatesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/mcgruder_rodney00.html | url-status = dead }} In his junior season, McGruder upped his scoring to 15.8 per game and made the second team All-Big 12. As a senior in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]], McGruder was a preseason All-Big 12 pick.{{cite web | title = McGruder named preseason All-Big 12 | work = TheMercury.com | date = October 4, 2012 | url = http://themercury.com/articles/mcgruder-named-preseason-all-big-12 | accessdate = March 3, 2013 | archive-date = March 1, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140301211527/http://themercury.com/articles/mcgruder-named-preseason-all-big-12 | url-status = dead }} He was also named a top 30 finalist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] on February 27, 2013.{{cite web | title = Naismith Award finalists announced | work = FoxSports.com | date = February 27, 2013 | url = http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Top-30-finalists-for-Naismith-Award-are-announced-022613 | accessdate = March 3, 2013 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20130302102733/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Top-30-finalists-for-Naismith-Award-are-announced-022613 | archivedate = March 2, 2013 }} During his senior season, McGruder led the Wildcats to a first-place finish in the Big XII. ==Professional career== ===Atomerőmű (2013–2014)=== After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], McGruder joined the Orlando Magic for the Orlando Summer League and the Charlotte Bobcats for the Las Vegas Summer League.{{Cite web|url=https://1350kman.com/mcgruder-to-play-with-bobcats/|title=McGruder to Play With Bobcats|date=July 15, 2013}} On September 27, 2013, he signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14344|title=OKC Thunder sign guards Diante Garrett and Rodney McGruder – NBA Blog|date=September 27, 2013 }} However, he was later waived by the Thunder on October 25, 2013.{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14633|title=OKC Thunder waive Diante Garrett and Rodney McGruder – NBA Blog|date=October 25, 2013 }} In November 2013, McGruder signed with [[Atomerőmű SE]] of Hungary for the 2013–14 season. In 29 league games for Atomerőmű, he averaged 14.4 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game. ===Maine Red Claws (2014–2015)=== In July 2014, McGruder joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. On September 29, 2014, he signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-training-camp-roster|title=Celtics Finalize Training Camp Roster|website=Boston Celtics}} However, he was later waived by the Celtics on October 27, 2014.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-opening-night-roster|title=Celtics Finalize Opening Night Roster|website=Boston Celtics}} Four days later, he was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/babb_is_back_2014_10_31.html | title=Red Claws Announce Affiliate Players, Returning Player Invitees | work=NBA.com | date=October 31, 2014 | accessdate=November 2, 2014 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150512002646/http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/babb_is_back_2014_10_31.html | archivedate=May 12, 2015 }} On March 26, 2015, he was waived by the Red Claws after appearing in 26 games.{{cite web | url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4942739 | title=Red Claws Acquire James Tyler | work=OurSportsCentral.com | date=March 26, 2015 | accessdate=March 26, 2015}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2015–2016)=== On March 29, 2015, McGruder was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web | url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4944527 | title=Sioux Falls Acquires Rodney McGruder | work=OurSportsCentral.com | date=March 30, 2015 | accessdate=March 30, 2015}} In July 2015, McGruder joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web|url=http://themercury.com/articles/mcgruder-playing-for-heat-in-summer|title=McGruder playing for Heat in summer|access-date=August 21, 2015|archive-date=May 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530095536/http://themercury.com/articles/mcgruder-playing-for-heat-in-summer|url-status=dead}} On November 2, 2015, he was reacquired by the Skyforce.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065971|title=Skyforce Announces 2015-16 Training Camp Roster|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 2, 2015|accessdate=November 4, 2015}} He helped the Skyforce finish with a D-League-best 40–10 record in 2015–16, and went on to help the team win the league championship with a 2–1 Finals series win over the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|title=Sioux Falls Skyforce Cap Historic Season with First NBA D-League|work=NBA.com|date=April 27, 2016|accessdate=April 28, 2016|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428121154/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160427/LADSXF/|url-status=dead}} ===Miami Heat (2016–2019)=== [[File:Rodney McGruder (31087687806) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|McGruder shoots while with the [[Miami Heat]] in 2016]] In July 2016, McGruder re-joined the Miami Heat for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information-1|title=HEAT Announce Summer League Information|website=Miami Heat}} On July 7, he signed a three-year, partially guaranteed contract with the Heat.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-rodney-mcgruder|title=HEAT Signs Rodney McGruder|website=Miami Heat}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/catzone/2016-07-07/former-k-state-basketball-player-rodney-mcgruder-signs-miami-heat|title=Former K-State basketball player Rodney McGruder signs with Miami Heat|first=The|last=Capital-Journal|website=The Topeka Capital-Journal}} He made his NBA debut in the Heat's season opener on October 26, 2016, against the [[Orlando Magic]]. In just under 24 minutes off the bench, he recorded six points, three rebounds and two steals in a 108–96 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899378|title=Heat vs. Magic – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} On February 6, 2017, he scored a season-high 15 points against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcgruro01/gamelog/2017/|title=Rodney McGruder 2016-17 Game Log|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=October 12, 2017}} On October 12, 2017, McGruder was ruled out indefinitely with a stress fracture in his left leg.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/10/12/miami-heat-rodney-mcgruder-out-indefinitely-stress-fracture-leg#/|title=Miami Heat's Rodney McGruder out indefinitely with stress fracture in leg|work=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2017|accessdate=October 12, 2017}} He made his season debut for the Heat on February 27, 2018, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] after playing two games for the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] just days prior.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975655|title=Father Prime: Wade gets 27, Heat beat 76ers 102-101|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2018|access-date=February 27, 2018}} On April 7, 2019, McGruder was waived by the Heat.{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-notebook-s20190407-story.html|title=Heat waive Rodney McGruder in tax move; sign Maten to NBA deal|work=sun-sentinel.com|date=April 7, 2019|accessdate=April 7, 2019}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2019–2020)=== On April 9, 2019, McGruder was claimed off waivers by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-claim-former-heat-forward-rodney-mcgruder-waivers|title=L.A. Clippers Claim Rodney McGruder Off Waivers|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2019|accessdate=April 9, 2019}} ===Detroit Pistons (2020–2023)=== On November 19, 2020, McGruder was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in a three-team trade that sent [[Justin Patton]] and [[Luke Kennard (basketball)|Luke Kennard]] to the Clippers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nets-acquire-shamet-from-clippers-in-3-team-trade|title=Nets acquire Shamet from Clippers in 3-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2020|accessdate=November 20, 2020}} On August 6, 2021, McGruder was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|title=Pistons Waives Rodney McGruder|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/pistons-waive-rodney-mcgruder.html|website=hoopsrumors.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On August 11, however, he re-signed with the Pistons.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Re-Sign Rodney McGruder|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-re-sign-rodney-mcgruder|date=August 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 11, 2021}} On January 10, 2022, McGruder was traded along with a 2022 second-round draft pick via the [[Brooklyn Nets]] to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Bol Bol]].{{Cite web|title=Nuggets Acquire Rodney McGruder|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-mcgruder-011022|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=NBA}} However, the trade was voided on January 13, 2022, after Bol failed his physical, leading to McGruder returning to the Pistons.{{Cite web|date=2022-01-13|title=Detroit Pistons void deal with Denver Nuggets for Bol Bol after failed physical|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33057585/sources-detroit-pistons-void-deal-denver-nuggets-bol-bol-failed-physical|access-date=2022-01-13|website=ESPN|language=en-US}} On August 1, 2022, McGruder re-signed with the Pistons.{{Cite web|date=2022-08-01|title=Pistons re-sign Rodney McGruder, finalize Kevin Knox deal|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/08/01/report-pistons-re-sign-rodney-mcgruder-finalize-kevin-knox-deal/10210067002/|access-date=2022-08-02|website=DetroitNews.com|language=en-US}} On September 28, 2023, McGruder signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]],{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Six Players to Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-six-players-to-contracts-20230928|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Rudy Gay and Rodney McGruder|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-rudy-gay-and-rodney-mcgruder-20231020|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} ===Olimpia Milano (2024)=== On January 10, 2024, McGruder signed with [[Olimpia Milano|EA7 Emporio Armani Milan]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=It is Hot Rod time: Rodney McGruder comes to Olimpia|url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/it-is-hot-rod-time-rodney-mcgruder-comes-to-olimpia/?prevpage=home|website=OlimpiaMilano.com|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2024}} On March 13, 2024, he parted ways with the Italian powerhouse due to a personal matter overseas.
